The JCT states that such a simple closed curve divides the plane into two disjoint regions: a bounded interior region ($I$) and an unbounded exterior region ($E$).
2. **Flooding Containment:** The flooding process occurs locally: a cell adjacent to a flooded cell becomes flooded only if there is no wall separating them.
3. **Victory Implication:** If the final barrier $L$ forms a simple closed loop and the set of all flooded cells $F$ is entirely contained within the bounded interior region $I$ (i.e., $F \subset I$), then $L$ acts as a complete topological boundary.
